preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(int(line.strip()), int) and 1 <= int(line.strip()) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: Each line in stdin is a positive integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^9), and the first line is T (1 ≤ T ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.
The input has exactly T + 1 lines: the first line is T, followed by T lines of N values.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout_line.strip()) == 1 and stdout_line.strip().isdigit() for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each line of stdout is a single integer representing the count of palindromes modulo 1000000007 for the corresponding N.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout_line.strip()) < 1000000007 for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a valid result modulo 1000000007.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout_line.strip()) == sum(26 ** ((k + 1) // 2) for k in range(1, int(N_line) + 1)) % 1000000007 for N_line, stdout_line in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each N in the input, the output is the sum over k from 1 to N of 26 raised to the power of ceil(k / 2), modulo 1000000007. This counts all palindromes of length ≤ N: for odd lengths (k), the first ceil(k / 2) characters determine the rest; for even lengths, the first k / 2 characters determine the rest.
